bottom_line: In high-risk patients, ramipril vs placebo reduced the primary composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (relative risk, 0.78; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.86).
implications: These data support that, in this trial population, assigning ramipril rather than placebo reduced the risk of the primary composite outcome (14.0% vs 17.8%; relative risk, 0.78; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.70 to 0.86) and reduced several individual outcomes (e.g., death from cardiovascular causes 6.1% vs 8.1%; myocardial infarction 9.9% vs 12.3%; stroke 3.4% vs 4.9%). The results also show higher discontinuation for cough with ramipril (7.3% vs 1.8%). The document does not provide evidence here about effects outside the studied eligibility criteria or beyond the follow-up described.

major_points.text: Double-blind, two-by-two factorial randomized trial evaluating ramipril and vitamin E.
major_points.quote: The double-blind, two-by-two factorial, randomized Heart Outcomes Prevention Evaluation study evaluated ramipril and vitamin E in 9541 patients.

major_points.text: High-risk patients aged 55 years or older with vascular disease or diabetes plus another cardiovascular risk factor were enrolled; those with known low EF or heart failure were excluded.
major_points.quote: A total of 9297 high-risk patients (55 years of age or older) who had evidence of vascular disease or diabetes plus one other cardiovascular risk factor and who were not known to have a low ejection fraction or heart failure

major_points.text: Intervention was ramipril 10 mg once daily vs matching placebo, with mean follow-up of five years.
major_points.quote: assigned to receive ramipril (10 mg once per day orally) or matching placebo for a mean of five years.

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
major_points.quote: The primary study outcome was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: Primary composite endpoint occurred in 14.0% with ramipril vs 17.8% with placebo (relative risk 0.78; 95% CI 0.70–0.86; P<0.001).
More patients stopped treatment for cough with ramipril than placebo (7.3% vs 1.8%).

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses were conducted using tests for interactions in Cox regression model.
subgroups.quote: Subgroup analyses were conducted with the use of tests for interactions in the Cox regression model.

subgroups.text: Benefit was consistently observed among predefined subgroups including diabetes status, sex, age, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, and microalbuminuria.
subgroups.quote: among the following predefined subgroups: patients with diabetes and those without diabetes, women and men, those with evidence of cardiovascular disease and those without such evidence, those younger than 65

subgroups.text: Among patients with documented ejection fraction of 0.40 or greater: 332/2379 vs 451/2393 (relative risk 0.73; 95% CI 0.63 to 0.84; P<0.001).
subgroups.quote: documented ejection fraction of 0.40 or greater (332 of 2379 patients reached the end point in the ramipril group vs. 451 of 2393 patients in the placebo group; relative risk, 0.73;

harms.text: Discontinuation at any time occurred in 32.5% with ramipril vs 30.7% with placebo.
Cough as a reason for stopping: 7.3% ramipril vs 1.8% placebo.
Hypotension or dizziness as a reason for stopping: 1.9% ramipril vs 1.5% placebo.
Angioedema as a reason for stopping: 0.4% ramipril vs 0.2% placebo.

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and women at least 55 years old.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Men and women who were at least 55 years old were eligible for the study

inclusion_criteria.text: History of coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetes plus at least one other cardiovascular risk factor.
inclusion_criteria.quote: if they had a history of coronary artery disease, stroke, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetes plus at least one other cardiovascular risk factor

exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded if they had heart failure
were known to have a low ejection fraction (<0.40)

exclusion_criteria.text: Taking an angiotensin-converting–enzyme inhibitor or vitamin E.
exclusion_criteria.quote: were taking an angiotensin-converting–enzyme inhibitor or vitamin E
had uncontrolled hypertension or overt nephropathy

exclusion_criteria.text: Myocardial infarction or stroke within four weeks before the study began.
exclusion_criteria.quote: or had had a myocardial infarction or stroke within four weeks before the study began.

analysis_methods.quote: study to have 90 percent power to detect a 13.5 percent reduction in the relative risk with a two-sided alpha level of 0.05 and with data analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis.

analysis_methods.text: Survival curves estimated using Kaplan–Meier and compared with log-rank test.
analysis_methods.quote: Survival curves were estimated according to the Kaplan–Meier procedure, and treat- ments were compared with use of the log-rank test.

analysis_methods.text: Because of factorial design, analyses were stratified for randomization to vitamin E or placebo.
analysis_methods.quote: Because of the factorial design, all analyses were stratified for the randomization to vitamin E or placebo.
